page_title: Mimer — Fast, private, developer-first clipboard manager for macOS

summary.name: Mimer
summary.one_liner: Mimer is a free, open-source, developer-focused clipboard manager for macOS with a ⇧⌘V command palette, type-aware history, and encrypted local storage.
use_cases: Recovering recently copied code, links, or text from clipboard history
Transforming copied text (case, Base64, URL encoding, JSON formatting) before pasting
Opening a commit, issue key, or file:line from a copied reference
Queuing several clips and pasting them in order
Keeping copied passwords and secrets out of screenshares and encrypted at rest
summary.what_it_does: Mimer records everything copied on macOS into a newest-first history that survives restarts, including images. It classifies clips by type (links, code, hex colors with a swatch, git SHAs, issue keys, file paths and stack-trace file:line references) and shows a matching glyph. A ⌘K menu offers live-preview transforms such as case changes, slugify, Base64/URL encoding, JSON pretty-printing, JSON to TypeScript, JWT decoding, and Unix/ISO time conversion. Scoped search (type:, app:, /regex/), a paste-stack, and ⌘O to open commits, issues, or file:line references in a browser, tracker, or editor are also included. History is encrypted at rest with AES-GCM using a key stored in the Keychain.
notable: Type-aware history with glyphs and live color swatches for links, code, git SHAs, issue keys and file:line
⌘K transforms with live preview, shown only when applicable
Imports Maccy history including timestamps, source apps and pinned items; Maccy's data is copied and never changed
History encrypted at rest (AES-GCM, key in Keychain) and detected secrets masked on screen
caveats: Auto-paste requires granting one system permission; otherwise the clip is only placed on the clipboard for manual ⌘V
Maccy import is the only migration path described
